content.comment_body: Hello all, Last year I set up a project that involved a [product_name] controller and an HMI from another manufacturer, using [product_name] engineering software and a third-party HMI platform. Currently, I'm considering using a more compact controller to manage lighting in a commercial building. While I find the smaller controller well-suited for building management tasks, the more advanced controller seemed unnecessary for this application. My challenge now is adapting to the newer configuration software and setting up data tags between the compact controller and HMI. I'm using a PC-based HMI runtime simulator, which is compatible with the third-party HMI platform. My goal is to trigger an output on the controller using a pushbutton on the HMI, mapped to a memory flag. Compared to my previous project, this setup feels more complicated. Does anyone have suggestions or experience with a similar setup? Thanks in advance.

Hello [user_name], Were you able to solve this issue? I'm facing similar challenges and would appreciate it if you could share any solutions or advice if you've figured it out. Thanks in advance! Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report difficulty moving from a more advanced controller system with established engineering tools to a compact controller and new configuration software when integrating with third-party HMIs. The process of configuring data tags and memory flags for basic control functions is not as intuitive as in previous setups, resulting in a steeper learning curve and user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope the setup of the compact controller with HMI should be as easy and flexible as their experience with previous controllers and engineering platforms, particularly in terms of tag data management and output control via HMIs.
